newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr seen range-bound before U.S. job data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr seen range-bound before U.S. job data.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be range-bound against the yen and the mark with a soft bias in Asia on Friday ahead of the release of U.S. May job data due out at 1230 GMT, dealers said.
Mark sales for yen overnight put pressure on the dollar/yen rate, but dealers doubtful that further mark selling will take place here and that such sales will drag on dollar/yen rate.
The mark fell as low as around 66.80 yen overnight after breaking through a tough support level at 67.00 yen.
"Mark/yen sales are done, so don't expect the mark to keep falling, at least in Tokyo," said a Japanese bank trader.
However, uncertainty over Europe's single currency plans could keep the weak mark trend intact.
If the mark falls clearly below 66.80 yen, the next target would be around 66.50 yen, said the Japanese bank trader.
Such a fall in the mark/yen would lead to sales in the dollar/yen, pushing it down to around 115.00 yen.
The mark was standing at 66.86/89 yen at 2314 GMT.

A trust bank dealer said the dollar was unlikely to move much in Asia ahead of the U.S. job data. According to the latest Reuters poll, Wall Street economists are forecasting a rise of 219,000 non-farm jobs in May.
The unemployment rate is expected to increase to 5.0 percent from a 23-year low of 4.9 percent last month, and average hourly earnings are seen rising 0.4 percent in May.

If the nonfarm payrolls come in as strong as expected, the dollar could get a boost against the mark, said the trust bank dealer. "The focus after the job data is on whether the dollar will rise above 1.7300 marks or fall below 115 yen," he said.
Persistent selling demand by exporters and investors on rises would make the dollar's recovery dull, making it difficult to reach 116 yen today, dealers said.
